# System Requirements Specification: Elite-Style Space Trading and Combat Game

Status: draft

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Purpose

This SRS defines the HOW contract for the Elite-Style Space Trading and Combat Game. It specifies the architectural structure, module responsibilities, invariants, test strategy, and the decomposition of every accepted acceptance criterion into implementation and verification bindings.

### 1.2 Scope

Single-player, browser-based Elite-style space trading and combat game served by a local Node.js HTTP server. Fully offline, zero build steps, playable in Google Chrome.

### 1.3 References

- PRD (id=2): `docs/requirements/REQ-001/02-prd.md`
- FR (id=3): `docs/requirements/REQ-001/03-functional-requirements.md`
- NFR (id=4): `docs/requirements/REQ-001/04-non-functional-requirements.md`

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Architectural Style

**Style:** Modular monolith.

**Rationale:** The brief classifies this product as XS complexity with sequence topology and `shared_mutation_risk: false`. The game is single-player, single-server, with no concurrency and all state local to one browser session. The gameplay is a sequential loop (dock, trade, jump, fight, dock) with no fanout. A modular monolith exposes stable seams and ownership boundaries without the indirection cost of ports/hexagonal/clean architecture, which is not justified by the actual topology or mutation risk.

### 2.2 Module Manifest

| Module | Responsibility | Owned Files |
|--------|---------------|-------------|
| server | Node.js HTTP server, static file serving, /healthz endpoint | server.js |
| game-state | Game state creation, initial conditions (100 credits, docked, small cargo), state shape contract | public/js/game-state.js |
| galaxy | Star system definitions (>= 8 named systems), station data, inter-system distances | public/js/galaxy.js |
| market | Per-system commodity pricing, buy/sell transaction execution, credit mutation | public/js/market.js |
| navigation | Hyperspace jump execution, fuel consumption calculation, pirate encounter trigger | public/js/navigation.js |
| combat | Arcade combat engine, enemy AI behavior, damage model, victory/defeat/escape resolution | public/js/combat.js |
| ship | Ship upgrades (cargo, laser, shields, fuel tank), upgrade purchase logic, attribute mutation | public/js/ship.js |
| rating | Elite rating tier calculation, accumulated profit tracking, kill count contribution | public/js/rating.js |
| persistence | Game state serialization to JSON, deserialization, save/load round-trip integrity | public/js/persistence.js |
| renderer | Canvas 2D rendering pipeline, parallax starfield, hyperspace effect, docking screen, combat visuals, HUD | public/js/renderer.js |
| ui | Screen state management, keyboard/mouse input handling, DOM manipulation, market display | public/js/ui.js |

### 2.3 Invariant Registry

| ID | Predicate | Check Level | Module |
|----|-----------|-------------|--------|
| INV-1 | `cargo_quantity <= cargo_capacity` always | L0, L2, L3 | ship |
| INV-2 | `credits >= 0` always; transactions are atomic | L0, L2 | market, ship |
| INV-3 | `fuel_consumed > 0` for any jump with `distance > 0` | L2, L3 | navigation |
| INV-4 | `fuel_consumed(distance_a) <= fuel_consumed(distance_b)` when `distance_a <= distance_b` | L2, L3 | navigation |
| INV-5 | `kill_count` is monotonically non-decreasing | L2, L3 | combat, rating |
| INV-6 | `accumulated_profit` is monotonically non-decreasing | L2, L3 | market, rating |
| INV-7 | `rating_tier(profit_after, kills_after) >= rating_tier(profit_before, kills_before)` when both inputs increase | L2, L3 | rating |
| INV-8 | A rejected transaction (insufficient credits, insufficient fuel, cargo overflow) leaves all state unchanged | L2, L3 | market, navigation, ship |

### 2.4 Port Registry

No inter-process or shared-boundary ports exist. The product is a sequential modular monolith with a single client-server HTTP boundary. Internal module communication is via direct function calls within the browser JS runtime.

| Contract | Direction | Protocol | Owner |
|----------|-----------|----------|-------|
| Static asset serving | Server -> Browser | HTTP GET | server |
| /healthz | Server -> Operator | HTTP GET, returns 200 | server |
| Save/load (optional) | Browser <-> Server | HTTP POST/GET | server, persistence |

All game logic modules execute in the browser. The server is a static file server with an optional save/load endpoint.

## 3. Technology Stack

### 3.1 Runtime

- **Server:** Node.js (LTS), zero external runtime dependencies beyond `npm install`
- **Client:** Google Chrome, vanilla JavaScript (ES2020+), Canvas 2D API
- **No bundler, no transpiler, no framework, no external CDN**

### 3.2 Project Structure

```
server.js                  # HTTP server + /healthz
package.json
public/
  index.html               # Game HTML shell
  js/
    main.js                # Client entry point
    game-state.js          # State creation, initial conditions
    galaxy.js              # Star system data, distances
    market.js              # Commodity pricing, transactions
    navigation.js          # Hyperspace jumps, fuel, encounters
    combat.js              # Combat engine, enemy AI
    ship.js                # Ship upgrades, cargo management
    rating.js              # Elite rating progression
    persistence.js         # Save/load serialization
    renderer.js            # Canvas 2D rendering, effects
    ui.js                  # Screen management, input
test/
  market.test.js           # Market pricing and transaction tests
  navigation.test.js       # Fuel/jump math tests
  combat.test.js           # Combat resolution tests
  persistence.test.js      # Save/load serialization tests
  smoke.js                 # Browser smoke test
```

## 4. Test Strategy and Reachability

### 4.1 Test Layers

| Layer | Runner | Reach | Command |
|-------|--------|-------|--------|
| L0 | Human | Full product in Chrome | Manual: `npm start` then play |
| L1 | Node.js test runner | Pure logic modules (market, navigation, combat, persistence) | `npm test` |
| L2 | Node.js test runner | Scenario-level tests for all invariants | `npm test` |
| L3 | Node.js test runner | Property-based tests for mathematically expressible invariants | `npm test` |

### 4.2 Runnable Commands

- `npm install` — install dependencies
- `npm start` — start the game server
- `npm test` — run all unit, scenario, and property-based tests
- `npm run smoke` — browser smoke test: starts server, loads page, asserts canvas renders

### 4.3 Test Reachability

L1/L2/L3 tests import pure-logic modules directly via `require()`. The modules use a dual-format pattern: `if (typeof module !== 'undefined') module.exports = ...` for Node.js compatibility while exposing functions on `window` for the browser. This ensures the same code exercised by `npm test` runs in the browser without a bundler.

The renderer and ui modules are browser-only (Canvas 2D, DOM) and are verified at L0 (human acceptance) and via the L1 smoke test that asserts canvas element creation.

## 5. Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Station | A docking point within a star system where the player can trade and buy upgrades |
| Hyperspace Jump | Travel between star systems consuming fuel proportional to distance |
| Cargo Capacity | Maximum total quantity of commodities the ship can hold |
| Elite Rating | Player rank determined by accumulated profit and combat kills |
| Pirate Encounter | Random event triggered after a hyperspace jump presenting fight-or-flee choice |

## 6. Out of Scope

- Multiplayer or networked gameplay
- Deployment to hosting environments
- Mobile browser support
- External CDN dependencies
- Docker containerization
- Database-backed persistence
- WebGL rendering (Canvas 2D is the baseline)

## 7. Supporting Systems

None. The product operates fully offline after `npm install`.

## 8. External Integrations

None. No external APIs, services, or network requests at runtime.

## 9. Security

No active security surfaces exist. The product is a local single-player game with no authentication, no user data beyond local save files, and no network exposure beyond localhost.

| Axis | Assessment | Reason |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Authentication | N/A | No user accounts |
| Authorization | N/A | Single-player, no roles |
| Input validation | Handled | Server validates only /healthz; client validates all game transactions |
| Data protection | N/A | No sensitive data |
| Network security | N/A | Localhost only, no external requests |

## 10. External Boundaries

| Boundary | Protocol | Trust Model | Failure Mode |
|----------|----------|-------------|-------------|
| Server -> Browser | HTTP (localhost) | Trusted local | Server not running: game inaccessible |
| Browser -> Server (save/load) | HTTP POST/GET (localhost) | Trusted local | File system write failure: save fails gracefully |

## §12 Decision Log

| # | Decision | Source/profile | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Date |
|---|----------|----------------|-------------------------|-----------|------|
| 1 | Modular monolith over hexagonal/ports | Brief complexity profile (XS, sequence, no shared mutation) | Hexagonal, clean architecture, ports and adapters | Sequential single-player game with no concurrency or shared boundaries does not justify port indirection | 2026-08-25 |
| 2 | Canvas 2D as rendering baseline | Inherited (brief assumption), deferred ord-c-001 | WebGL, WebGL2 | Canvas 2D is the stated PRD baseline; WebGL is optional fallback if 60fps target is not met. Decision deferred to development per brief disposition. | 2026-08-25 |
| 3 | localStorage for persistence | Inherited (brief assumption), deferred ord-c-002 | Server-side file storage, IndexedDB | localStorage is simplest for single-session browser game. Decision deferred to development per brief disposition. | 2026-08-25 |
| 4 | Dual-format modules (require + window) | Local | ES modules, bundler, global-only | Ensures test reachability from Node.js while maintaining zero-build browser loading | 2026-08-25 |
| 5 | No internal port contracts | Local (complexity gate) | Explicit function-contract ports | XS sequential monolith: internal module boundaries are function calls, not inter-process contracts | 2026-08-25 |

## §D1 Canonical File/Module Surface

| Module | Files | Public Surface |
|--------|-------|---------------|
| server | server.js | startServer(port), /healthz route |
| game-state | public/js/game-state.js | createNewGame(): GameState, loadGame(json): GameState |
| galaxy | public/js/galaxy.js | SYSTEMS: System[], getDistance(origin, destination): number |
| market | public/js/market.js | getMarket(system): Commodity[], buy(state, commodity, qty): TransactionResult, sell(state, commodity, qty): TransactionResult |
| navigation | public/js/navigation.js | calculateFuel(distance): number, executeJump(state, destination): JumpResult |
| combat | public/js/combat.js | startCombat(state): CombatState, resolveTurn(combatState, playerAction): CombatResult |
| ship | public/js/ship.js | getUpgrades(): Upgrade[], purchaseUpgrade(state, upgrade): TransactionResult |
| rating | public/js/rating.js | calculateRating(profit, kills): RatingTier |
| persistence | public/js/persistence.js | serialize(state): string, deserialize(json): GameState |
| renderer | public/js/renderer.js | init(canvas), renderFrame(state, screen), cleanup() |
| ui | public/js/ui.js | init(renderer), showScreen(screen), handleInput(event) |

## §D3 Priority Rationale

All ACs are classified as `blocker` except AC-18 (degradable). AC-18 targets 60fps on a 2020-era laptop; the game is functional at lower frame rates with degraded experience. All other ACs represent core gameplay mechanics or hard requirements from the PRD.

## §D4 Decomposition Pattern per Module Cluster

### Cluster: Game Foundation

Modules: game-state, galaxy, server

These modules establish the game world and initial state. AC-1 (galaxy map) and AC-2 (starting conditions) are the foundation upon which all gameplay depends.

### Cluster: Trading Economy

Modules: market, ship

Buy/sell and cargo management form a tight cluster sharing INV-1 (cargo bounds) and INV-2 (credit non-negativity). AC-3 through AC-6 are interdependent.

### Cluster: Navigation and Combat

Modules: navigation, combat

Jumps trigger encounters; encounters trigger combat. AC-7 through AC-11 form a sequential chain. INV-3, INV-4 (fuel) and INV-5 (kills) are owned here.

### Cluster: Progression

Modules: rating, ship (upgrades)

Rating depends on profit and kills from trading and combat. AC-12, AC-13, AC-14.

### Cluster: Persistence and Operations

Modules: persistence, server

Save/load and server health. AC-15, AC-16, AC-22.

### Cluster: Visual Presentation

Modules: renderer, ui

Canvas rendering and screen management. AC-17, AC-18.

### Cluster: Verification

No dedicated implementation module. Test files verify the implementation clusters. AC-19, AC-20, AC-21.
